","type":"text/x-markdown"},"/home/runner/work/tw-plugin-library/tw-plugin-library/wiki/plugins/rimir/dashboard/README.md":{"title":"/home/runner/work/tw-plugin-library/tw-plugin-library/wiki/plugins/rimir/dashboard/README.md","text":"# tw-dashboard A TiddlyWiki 5 plugin (`$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard`) that turns any tiddler into a **free-form dashboard**: a canvas onto which you drop other tiddlers as freely arrangeable tiles. ## What it does - Tag a tiddler with `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard` and its body becomes a canvas. - **Add tiles** by dragging tiddlers onto the canvas from anywhere in the wiki, or by typing a title and pressing *Add tile*. - **Batch-add by filter** — type a filter in the box above the canvas and press *Add matching* to drop a tile for every tiddler it selects, arranged in a grid. - **Clean** — remove tiles in one go (with a confirmation). Leave the clean filter empty to clear the whole dashboard, or give a filter to remove only the tiles whose target it selects. - **Move** a tile by dragging its title bar; **resize** it from the bottom-right corner. Geometry is saved on release. - **Bring-to-front** — interacting with a tile raises it; the `z`-order persists. - **Two styles** per tile: a *window* tile with a title bar, or a *bare* tile that is just the resizable content. - **Group (meta) tiles** — *Add group* creates a container tile that is itself a mini-canvas: drop tiddlers into it, drag existing tiles in and out, and nest groups inside groups recursively. Collapse to a header bar with ▸/▾, rename inline, and see the child count. Removing a group promotes its contents to the parent container. - **Click to open** — a click (not a drag) opens the tile's target tiddler in the story river. - **Ctrl-drag to duplicate** — hold Ctrl (or Cmd) as you start dragging a tile to drop a *copy* of it elsewhere (even into another group), leaving the original in place. The same tiddler can appear on as many tiles as you like. - **Show contents in a popup** — the ⧉ control opens the target in a centered popup rendered through TiddlyWiki's default ViewTemplate (title, tags, fields and body), without leaving the dashboard. Close it with the × button or by clicking the backdrop. - **Kind-aware** — when a tile's target is a [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind) instance, the window tile shows the type's icon (with the type name as hover text) before the caption. Degrades silently when kind isn't installed. ## Quick start 1. Click **New dashboard** in the page controls (right sidebar → Tools), or tag any tiddler `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard`. 2. Drag a few tiddlers onto the canvas. 3. Move, resize, and restyle them; click one to open it. ## Storage Each tile is its own system tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile`, stored under `$:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/…` with plain fields (`target`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, `style`). No JSON blobs — every mutation is an ordinary `$action-setfield`. ## Requirements TiddlyWiki >= 5.4.0. No other plugin dependencies. Rich documentation renders when [`rimir/doc-template`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-doc-template) is installed. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). Regions (matched via closest() on the pointerdown target): .rr-dash-no-drag never starts anything (buttons, links, inputs) .rr-dash-resize starts a resize drag move-selector starts a move drag; when the `move-selector` attribute is empty the whole box is a move surface (bare tiles) Move / resize move the DOM directly for smoothness and commit ONCE on release via the `actions` string (variables new-x / new-y / new-w / new-h) — never per pointermove, to avoid async write races. A pointerdown+up on a move surface with no motion beyond DRAG_THRESHOLD is a CLICK: it invokes `open-actions` instead (used to open the tile's target in the story river). Geometry commits also carry a fresh `z` so the tile comes to the front; the widget renders `z-index` from the `z` attribute. Reparenting: on release after a MOVE, the drop point is hit-tested against the `.rr-dash-canvas` elements (the widget hides itself with visibility:hidden so elementFromPoint sees the canvas beneath). If the topmost canvas under the pointer differs from the tile's current container — and belongs to the same dashboard and is not the tile's own descendant — the `reparent-actions` string is invoked with the extra `new-parent` variable and coordinates relative to the target canvas. Otherwise the ordinary `actions` (geometry) commit runs. `fit-width="yes"` / `fit-height="yes"` render the box at auto (shrink-to-fit) width / height — used for collapsed group tiles, which shrink to their header; the stored `w`/`h` are preserved (not applied) and restored on expand. The body-cascade swap A dashboard is an ordinary tiddler tagged <>. The plugin ships a `ViewTemplateBodyFilter` step, `$:/config/ViewTemplateBodyFilters/rimir-dashboard`, ordered `list-before` the `default` step: ``` [tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard]then[$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/body]] ``` So when a dashboard tiddler is viewed, its body renders `$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/body` — the canvas — while its title, tags and fields render through the normal ViewTemplate. Nothing else about the tiddler is special. !! Tiles are tiddlers Each tile is its own tiddler tagged <>, stored under a system-tiddler prefix: ``` $:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/ ``` `` is the dashboard's `dashboard-id` field (auto-generated for dashboards made with the //New dashboard// button) or, as a fallback, the dashboard's title. Tiles carry plain fields — `dashboard`, `target`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, `style` — so every operation is a plain `$action-createtiddler` / `$action-setfield` / `$action-deletetiddler`. There is no JSON serialisation to parse or rebuild, and the compact numeric fields keep the tiddlers in single-file `.tid` form. The canvas enumerates its tiles with: ``` [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboardnsort[z]] ``` Rendering in `z` order means DOM order and `z-index` agree. !! Groups and recursion A group (meta) tile is an ordinary tile with `role: group` and no `target`. Its body is a nested canvas. Membership is a single plain field: a tile's `dash-parent` holds the title of the group it lives in, and top-level tiles simply have no `dash-parent`. That makes the tiles of one dashboard a //tree//, and the canvas renders it with one recursive procedure: ``` dash-canvas(containerId) → lists tiles in that container → dash-tile dash-tile (role=group) → header + dash-canvas(thisGroupTitle) ← recurses ``` Each container is enumerated by the same shape of filter, differing only in the membership test — top-level uses `!has[dash-parent]`, a group uses `field:dash-parent`: ``` [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboard!has[dash-parent]nsort[z]] [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboardfield:dash-parentnsort[z]] ``` Because a child positions itself absolutely within its group's own `.rr-dash-canvas` (which is `position: relative`), the existing pixel-geometry model works unchanged at every level of nesting. Collapsing a group is just a `collapsed` field: when set, the body (and thus the whole subtree) is not rendered and the box is drawn at auto width //and// height, so it shrinks to its header; the stored `w`/`h` are preserved and reapplied on expand. Expanding also bumps the group's `z` to the front (guarded on the pre-toggle state) so its contents are not hidden behind sibling tiles. Removing a group re-homes its direct children to the group's own `dash-parent` — no recursive delete, no orphans. !! Re-parenting by drag Tiles (and whole groups) move between containers by dragging. The pointer-based tile drag is independent of the HTML5 drop used for adding tiddlers from the wiki, so the two never collide. On release after a move, the widget hit-tests the drop: # it captures the tile's on-screen rectangle, then hides itself with `visibility: hidden` so `document.elementFromPoint` reports the canvas //beneath// the tile rather than the tile itself; # it walks up from that element to the nearest `.rr-dash-canvas`, reading its `data-dash-parent` (the target container id) and `data-dash-id`; # if the target differs from the tile's current container, belongs to the same dashboard, and is not the tile's own descendant, it invokes `reparent-actions` with `<>` plus coordinates recomputed relative to the target canvas. Otherwise it commits geometry in place. Hiding the tile during the hit-test also gives cycle-safety for free: a group dropped onto its own contents resolves to the canvas behind it — its current container — so it simply does not reparent. !! The `<$dashboard-drag>` widget Free-form pointer dragging is the one thing wikitext cannot express, so a single JS widget owns it. It renders an absolutely-positioned box from `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`/`z` attributes and handles pointer interaction: * ''move'' starts on a `.rr-dash-handle` descendant (window tiles) or anywhere on the box when `move-selector` is empty (bare tiles); * ''resize'' starts on a `.rr-dash-resize` descendant; * elements marked `.rr-dash-no-drag` (buttons, the controls cluster) never start a drag. During a drag the DOM node is moved directly for smoothness. The geometry is written back exactly once, on pointer release, by invoking the `actions` string — a plain `$action-setfield` on the tile tiddler. Committing on release rather than on every pointermove avoids the async write races that come from saving on each interaction event. A pointerdown+up with no motion beyond a small threshold is treated as a ''click'' and invokes `open-actions` instead (used to navigate the target into the story river). Move and resize commits also recompute `z = max(sibling z) + 1`, giving bring-to-front behaviour. When a move ends over a different container the widget invokes `reparent-actions` instead of `actions` (see //Re-parenting by drag// above), and `fit-width`/`fit-height="yes"` make it render at auto (shrink-to-fit) size for collapsed groups. !! The contents popup The ⧉ tile control writes the target's title into `$:/state/rimir/dashboard/popup`. A single `<$reveal>` — rendered once at the canvas root, not per tile — watches that state and, when it is non-empty, shows a fixed-position overlay containing the target rendered through the default `$:/core/ui/ViewTemplate`: ``` <$tiddler tiddler={{$:/state/rimir/dashboard/popup}}> <$transclude $tiddler="$:/core/ui/ViewTemplate" $mode="block"/> ``` The overlay is `position: fixed` so it escapes the tile's `overflow` clipping and sits above every tile (whose `z-index` tops out at 9999 during a drag). The backdrop and the × button both clear the state tiddler to close. Because the state lives under `$:/state`, it is transient and never written to disk. !! Division of labour Everything except the pointer maths is wikitext and CSS: the cascade entry, the canvas body, the tile chrome, drop-to-add via the core `<$droppable>` widget, and the action strings that mutate tile fields. The widget is deliberately thin — it computes geometry and delegates all state writes back to wikitext. Create a dashboard Either click ''New dashboard'' in the sidebar Tools, or tag any existing tiddler: ``` title: My Board tags: $:/tags/rimir/dashboard dashboard-id: my-board ``` The `dashboard-id` is optional; without it the dashboard's title is used to group its tiles. The //New dashboard// button generates a timestamp id automatically. !! Add a tile by hand Tiles are plain tiddlers. This is exactly what //Add tile// and drop-to-add create: ``` title: $:/config/rimir/dashboard/my-board/tiles/tile tags: $:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile dashboard: my-board target: Some Interesting Tiddler style: window x: 32 y: 32 w: 340 h: 220 z: 1 ``` `dashboard` must match the dashboard's `dashboard-id` (or title). `target` is the tiddler the tile shows. !! A bare tile Set `style: bare` for a chrome-less tile — no title bar, the whole box is the drag/open surface, and the content is shown as a non-interactive preview: ``` title: $:/config/rimir/dashboard/my-board/tiles/tile-1 tags: $:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile dashboard: my-board target: A Chart Or Image style: bare x: 400 y: 90 w: 320 h: 240 z: 2 ``` You can flip any tile between //window// and //bare// live with the ⊟ control (in the title bar for window tiles, in the hover corner for bare tiles). !! A group (meta) tile Press ''Add group'' to create a container tile. A group has `role: group`, no `target`, and its body is a canvas for other tiles: ``` title: $:/config/rimir/dashboard/my-board/tiles/group tags: $:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile role: group dashboard: my-board caption: Research collapsed: no x: 40 y: 40 w: 360 h: 300 z: 1 ``` A tile belongs to a group when its `dash-parent` field holds the group's title: ``` title: $:/config/rimir/dashboard/my-board/tiles/tile-in-group tags: $:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile dashboard: my-board dash-parent: $:/config/rimir/dashboard/my-board/tiles/group target: A Source x: 16 y: 16 w: 220 h: 140 ``` Give a child the title of a //group// (via `dash-parent`) and that group renders inside its parent — nesting is recursive. In practice you rarely edit these by hand: type a name in the add box and press ''Add group'' (the text becomes the group's `caption`), drop tiddlers into it, and use the group's ＋ control to add a nested group. You can rename a group inline from its header at any time. !! Batch-add by filter The filter box above the canvas adds a tile for every tiddler a filter selects. For example, to tile every open task: ``` [tag[Task]!tag[Done]] ``` or every tiddler linking to the current project, every image, every member of a list — anything valid in a `<$list>` works (it is evaluated with `subfilter`). The matches are laid out in a grid (three columns) and the box is cleared afterwards. Tiles are always added; a matching tiddler that already has a tile simply gets another (see //Duplicate// below), so narrow the filter if you want to avoid repeats. !! Clean the dashboard The ''Clean'' button removes tiles after a confirmation that shows how many will go. The box next to it scopes what is removed: * ''empty'' → every tile on the dashboard, including groups. * ''a filter'' → only the tiles whose `target` the filter selects. For example `[tag[Archived]]` removes the tiles pointing at archived tiddlers and leaves the rest (groups, having no target, are never matched by a target filter). The filter is evaluated with `subfilter`, so any list filter works. The underlying tiddlers are never touched — only the tiles (the dashboard's references to them). !! Interacting * ''Move'' — drag the title bar (window / group) or anywhere on the tile (bare). * ''Resize'' — drag the bottom-right corner. * ''Bring to front'' — any move or resize raises the tile and persists its `z`. * ''Group / ungroup by dragging'' — drag a tile onto a group to move it inside; drag it back onto the root canvas (or another group) to re-home it. Whole groups move with their contents. * ''Collapse / expand'' — the ▸/▾ control on a group hides its contents and shrinks it to just the header (as narrow as its content); expanding restores its previous width and height //and brings the group to the front// so its contents aren't hidden behind other tiles. The header shows the child count and an editable name. * ''Open'' — click (without dragging) to open the target in the story river. * ''Duplicate'' — hold ''Ctrl'' (or ''Cmd'') as you start dragging a content tile to drop a copy of it where you release — in the same container or another one. The original stays put, and both tiles point at the same target tiddler. * ''Show contents'' — the ⧉ control opens the target in a centered popup rendered through the default ViewTemplate, without leaving the dashboard. Close it with × or by clicking the backdrop. * ''Remove'' — the × control on a content tile deletes that tile tiddler only; the target tiddler is untouched. The × on a group removes the group and promotes its contents to the parent container. !! Housekeeping filters List every dashboard: ``` [tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard]] ``` List a dashboard's tiles (highest on top last): ``` [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboard[my-board]nsort[z]] ``` Find orphaned tiles whose target no longer exists: ``` [tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]get[target]] :filter[!is[tiddler]] ``` "},"$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/doc/faq":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/doc/faq","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","rdt.order":"5","rdt.plugin-key":"dashboard","rdt.plugin-name":"dashboard","rdt.section":"FAQ","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Does the layout reflow on small screens? No. Tiles use absolute pixel coordinates, so a free-form dashboard is desktop-first and does not reflow to narrow viewports. This is inherent to the free-form model. !! A tile shows nothing / only raw text — why? A tile transcludes the target tiddler's body. Tiddlers whose visible display comes from ViewTemplate //segments// rather than their body — and stream-typed tiddlers, whose `text` field is empty — render thin in a tile. Point the tile at a tiddler with body content, or use a transclusion-bearing wrapper as the target. !! What is the difference between the ⧉ popup and clicking a tile to open it? Clicking a tile ''navigates'' to the target in the story river (leaving the dashboard view). The ⧉ //show contents// control instead opens the target in a centered popup ''on top of'' the dashboard, rendered through the default ViewTemplate — so you can read the full tiddler (title, tags, fields and body) without losing your place. Close it with × or by clicking the backdrop. !! Can the same tiddler appear on more than one tile? Yes. A tile is just a tiddler with a `target` field, so nothing stops several tiles — anywhere on the dashboard or across its groups — from pointing at the same target. The quickest way to make one is to hold ''Ctrl'' (or ''Cmd'') while you start dragging a tile: that drops a copy where you release instead of moving the original. !! How do I put tiles into a group, and nest groups? Press ''Add group'' for a container tile, then either drop tiddlers from the wiki onto its canvas or drag existing tiles into it. A group's ＋ control adds a group //inside// it, and you can also drag a whole group into another — nesting is recursive with no depth limit. Drag a tile (or group) back onto the root canvas to take it out again. !! I expanded a group but another tile covers it — how do I keep it on top? Expanding a group already raises it to the front (its `z` becomes the highest on the dashboard), so its contents sit above the other tiles. If you later move or resize a //different// tile, that tile comes to the front in turn and may overlap the group again — just click the group's ▾/▸ toggle (or move it) to raise it back. !! What happens to the tiles inside a group when I delete the group? They are not deleted. Removing a group (its × control) promotes its direct children up to the group's own container — so a group at the top level spills its contents onto the dashboard, and a nested group spills into its parent group. Delete the child tiles individually if you want them gone. !! Why did my tile snap to a new position when I dragged it into a group? Positions are relative to the container. When a tile moves into (or out of) a group its coordinates are recomputed relative to the new canvas, so it keeps roughly the on-screen spot where you dropped it rather than its old numbers. !! How do I switch a tile between window and bare? Use the ⊟ control — in the title bar of a window tile, or the hover-corner cluster of a bare tile. It toggles the tile's `style` field. !! Clicking a bare tile opens the tiddler instead of interacting with its content — is that expected? Yes. Bare tiles are previews: their content is non-interactive (`pointer-events: none`) so the whole box reliably acts as move / open surface. Use a window tile when you need to interact with the content. !! Where is my dashboard's layout stored? In the tile tiddlers under `$:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/…`. They sync to disk like any `$:/config` tiddler. Deleting a dashboard does not delete its tiles automatically — remove them by prefix if you want them gone. !! Do dashboards nest? You can point a tile at another dashboard tiddler; it will render that dashboard's canvas inside the tile. Deeply nested dashboards are untested — treat as an edge case. !! Can a tile show the kind type icon? Yes — automatically. If a window tile's target is a [[rimir/kind|$:/plugins/rimir/kind]] instance, the type's icon appears before the caption with the type name as hover text. It requires nothing beyond having kind installed and a `kind.icon` on the type; without kind, the icon is simply omitted. (Bare tiles have no title bar, so no icon is shown there.) !! Nothing happens when I drag — the tile just gets selected/dragged as text. That is a sign the drag region isn't arming (for example an element accidentally marked `.rr-dash-no-drag`). Move starts only on the handle (window) or the box (bare); resize only on the corner grip. What it does Turn any tiddler into a //dashboard//: a free-form canvas onto which you drop other tiddlers as freely arrangeable tiles. Each tile transcludes a target tiddler; you move it, resize it, restyle it, and click it to open the underlying tiddler in the story river. Tag a tiddler with <> and a view-template body cascade entry swaps its body for the dashboard canvas — no special editor, no separate app. !! Key features * ''Drop to add'' — drag any tiddler from the wiki onto the canvas and it becomes a tile. Or type a title and press //Add tile//. * ''Batch-add by filter'' — type any filter above the canvas and press //Add matching// to add a tile for each tiddler it selects, laid out in a grid. * ''Clean'' — remove all tiles (or only those whose target matches a filter) in one confirmed step. * ''Free-form layout'' — absolute pixel positioning; drag a tile to move, drag its bottom-right corner to resize. Geometry is saved on release. * ''Bring-to-front z-order'' — interacting with a tile raises it above the others; the stacking order persists. * ''Two tile styles'' — a //window// tile with a title bar and controls, or a //bare// tile that is just the resizable content. * ''Group (meta) tiles'' — a group tile is itself a free-form canvas you can drop other tiles into; groups nest recursively. Collapse/expand with ▸/▾, rename inline, and drag tiles (or whole groups) between containers to re-home them. * ''Click to open'' — a click (as opposed to a drag) opens the tile's target tiddler in the story river. * ''Ctrl-drag to duplicate'' — hold Ctrl/Cmd while starting a drag to drop a copy of the tile elsewhere (the same tiddler may appear on any number of tiles). * ''Show contents in a popup'' — the ⧉ control opens the target in a centered popup rendered through the default ViewTemplate (title, tags, fields and body), without leaving the dashboard. * ''Kind-aware'' — when a tile's target is a [[rimir/kind|$:/plugins/rimir/kind]] instance, the window tile shows the type's icon (with the type name as hover text) before the caption. Silently absent when kind is not installed. * ''Plain-field storage'' — every tile is its own system tiddler with ordinary editable fields (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, `target`, `style`). No JSON blobs. !! Quick start # Click ''New dashboard'' in the page controls (right sidebar → Tools), or tag any tiddler <>. # Drag a few tiddlers onto the canvas. # Move, resize, and restyle them; click one to open it. See the ''Examples'' tab for concrete recipes and ''Reference'' for the full field and tag list. Tile fields |!Field |!Meaning | |`dashboard` |The owning dashboard's id (or title) | |`target` |Title of the tiddler shown inside the tile (content tiles only) | |`dash-parent` |Title of the group tile this tile lives inside. Empty / absent = top-level (directly on the dashboard canvas) | |`role` |`group` for a group (meta) tile; empty / absent for an ordinary content tile | |`caption` |Group tiles only — the editable group name shown in its header | |`collapsed` |Group tiles only — `yes` shows just the header bar, otherwise the group's canvas is shown | |`x` / `y` |Top-left position in pixels, relative to the tile's container canvas | |`w` / `h` |Width / height in pixels (both are retained but not applied while a group is collapsed — it shrinks to its header — and restored on expand) | |`z` |Stacking order (higher = in front); set to `max+1` on interaction | |`style` |Content tiles only — `window` (default) or `bare` | !! Group (meta) tiles A tile with `role: group` is a container: its body is a nested `.rr-dash-canvas` enumerating the tiles whose `dash-parent` is this group's title. Because membership is a single field forming a tree, groups nest recursively with no depth limit. A group is positioned, dragged and resized like any tile; the ▸/▾ header control toggles `collapsed`, and its ＋ control adds a nested group. Removing a group re-homes its direct children to the group's own parent (they are not deleted). Tiles — including whole groups — are re-parented by ''dragging'' them onto another container: on release the drop point is hit-tested for the topmost `.rr-dash-canvas`, and if it differs from the tile's current container (and is the same dashboard, and not the tile's own descendant) the tile's `dash-parent`, position and `z` are rewritten. Holding ''Ctrl''/''Cmd'' at the start of the drag ''duplicates'' a content tile instead of moving it — a new tile with the same `target` is created at the drop point and the original is left untouched, so a tiddler may appear on any number of tiles. !! Tile title scheme ``` $:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/ ``` Tiles live under `$:/config/…`, so they sync to disk but stay out of the default tiddler lists. !! `<$dashboard-drag>` widget The positioning/interaction widget (used internally by the canvas body). |!Attribute |!Meaning | |`tile` |Title of the tile tiddler | |`x` `y` `w` `h` |Initial geometry in pixels | |`z` |Initial `z-index` | |`class` |Class(es) for the box element | |`move-selector` |CSS selector that starts a move; empty = the whole box | |`min-width` `min-height` |Resize floor (default 120 / 80) | |`fit-width` / `fit-height` |`yes` renders the box at auto (shrink-to-fit) width / height (used for collapsed groups, which shrink to their header); otherwise `w` / `h` are applied | |`container` |Id of the container this tile currently lives in (the group title, or empty for the root canvas) — used to detect re-parenting | |`dash-id` |The dashboard id — re-parenting is only allowed within the same dashboard | |`actions` |Action string invoked on a move/resize release //within the same container//, with variables `<>` `<>` `<>` `<>` | |`reparent-actions` |Action string invoked when a move ends over a //different// container, with the above plus `<>` (the target container's id) | |`copy-actions` |Action string invoked instead of moving when Ctrl/Cmd is held at the start of a move — same variables as `reparent-actions`. Creates a duplicate tile; the original snaps back. Only content tiles set this (groups are not duplicated) | |`open-actions` |Action string invoked on a click (no drag) | Recognised regions inside the box: `.rr-dash-handle` (move surface for window and group tiles), `.rr-dash-resize` (resize grip), `.rr-dash-no-drag` (never starts a drag — buttons, controls, the group-name input). Each `.rr-dash-canvas` carries `data-dash-parent` (its container id) and `data-dash-id` so the widget can hit-test drop targets. !! Kind integration (optional) When [[rimir/kind|$:/plugins/rimir/kind]] is installed and a window tile's `target` is a kind instance (a tiddler with a `kind.type` field), the title bar prefixes the caption with the type's `kind.icon`, using the type's `kind.caption` as hover text. Dashboard Turn any tiddler into a //dashboard//: a free-form canvas onto which you drop other tiddlers as freely-arrangeable tiles. !! What it does * Tag a tiddler with <> and its body becomes a canvas. * ''Add tiles'' by dragging tiddlers onto the canvas from anywhere in the wiki, or by typing a title and pressing //Add tile//. * ''Batch-add by filter'' — type a filter in the box above the canvas and press //Add matching// to drop a tile for every tiddler it selects, arranged in a grid. * ''Clean'' — remove tiles in one go (with a confirmation). Leave the clean filter empty to clear the whole dashboard, or give a filter to remove only the tiles whose target it selects. * ''Move'' a tile by dragging its title bar, ''resize'' it from the bottom-right corner — geometry is saved on release. * ''Bring-to-front'' — interacting with a tile raises it above the others, and the stacking order persists. * ''Two tile styles'' — a //window// tile with a title bar, or a //bare// tile that is just the resizable content. Toggle with the ⊟ control. In both styles the buttons appear only while you hover the tile and float over the title, so the caption keeps the full width. * ''Group (meta) tiles'' — press //Add group// for a container tile that is itself a mini-canvas: drop tiddlers into it, drag existing tiles in and out of it, and nest groups inside groups recursively. Whatever you type in the add box becomes the new group's name (you can also rename it inline later). Collapse a group with ▸/▾ and it shrinks to just its header bar (as narrow as its content); expanding restores its previous size and raises it to the front so its contents stay visible. Rename it inline and see its child count. Removing a group promotes its contents to the parent container. * ''Click to open'' — a click (as opposed to a drag) opens the tile's target tiddler in the story river. * ''Ctrl-drag to duplicate'' — hold Ctrl (or Cmd) as you start dragging a tile to drop a //copy// of it elsewhere (even into another group), leaving the original in place. The same tiddler can appear on as many tiles as you like. * ''Show contents in a popup'' — the ⧉ control opens the target in a centered popup rendered through TiddlyWiki's default ViewTemplate (title, tags, fields and body), without leaving the dashboard. Close it with the × button or by clicking the backdrop. * ''Kind-aware'' — when a tile's target is a [[rimir/kind|$:/plugins/rimir/kind]] instance, the window tile shows the type's icon (with the type name as hover text) before the caption. Degrades silently when kind is not installed. !! Quick start # Click //New dashboard// in the page controls (right sidebar → Tools), or tag any tiddler <>. # Drag a few tiddlers onto the canvas. # Move, resize, and restyle them; click one to open it. !! How it is stored Each tile is its own tiddler tagged <>, stored under `$:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/…` with plain fields (`target` / `x` / `y` / `w` / `h` / `z` / `style`). No JSON blobs — every move, resize or restyle is an ordinary `$action-setfield`. !! Prerequisites TiddlyWiki >= 5.4.0. No hard dependencies. Optional: [[rimir/kind|$:/plugins/rimir/kind]] (type icons on tiles) and [[rimir/doc-template|$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template]] (branded documentation).
